title: test_messages.py: RERR.error_code range check is untested; to_bytes & 0xFF makes it deletable
description:
ROBUSTNESS review of python/tests/loadng/test_messages.py (after 9098.10 independent-hex flags/hop).

messages.py RERR.to_bytes (lines 163-166) is the only encode-side bound that can be deleted without this file failing:

    if not 0 <= self.error_code <= 255:
        raise LoadngError(...)
    return bytes([self.flags & 0xFF, self.error_code & 0xFF]) + ...

Hop encode tests (test_rreq_hop_limit_range_validated, test_rrep_hop_count_range_validated) lock negative, 16, and edges 0/15. seq_num is locked only as RREQ(seq_num=0x10000) (test_seq_num_range_validated). error_code has no encode test at all: known/round-trip/hex/from_icmpv6 use 1 or 2.

Unlike seq_num, deleting the error_code check does not OverflowError. 256 & 0xFF and -1 & 0xFF silently encode as 0 and 255. A caller that passes 256 (or a computed code) puts Unspecified/0 on the wire instead of failing closed. test_vectors.py only has in-range 0/1/2/255, so it does not catch this either.

Same mask without a check on flags (RREQ/RREP/RERR to_bytes `self.flags & 0xFF`). This file never constructs flags outside 0..255, so flags=0x100 → 0 (all bits dropped) and flags=-1 → 255 stay green.

Secondary encode-range holes versus the hop tests in this file:
- RREP.seq_num 0x10000 is untested (only RREQ).
- seq_num=-1 is untested; a check that is only `> 0xFFFF` becomes OverflowError from to_bytes(2, "big"), not LoadngError.
- seq_num 0 and 0xFFFF are not locked here (0xFFFF is in loadng_messages.json / test_vectors.py; 0 is in neither).

Do not re-file 4a8y (to_bytes as parse oracle), 9098.8 (empty from_icmpv6 bodies), 9098.9 (sig tail 32/96), 9098.10 (RREQ hex defaults), or worker6-esp1 (to_bytes signature length).

Fix: add encode tests in this file that would fail if the error_code check were deleted or reduced to the mask — error_code=-1 and 256 raise LoadngError (match error_code); 0 and 255 encode and parse from a hand-built 18-byte body. Mirror hop tests for seq_num: RREQ and RREP, -1 and 0x10000 raise, 0 and 0xFFFF encode. Decide whether flags outside 0..255 should raise like error_code or stay masked, and lock that choice with a test.
close_reason: RERR.error_code -1/256 raise LoadngError (fail-closed, no &0xFF mask); flags 0..255 same on RREQ/RREP/RERR; RREQ+RREP seq_num -1/0x10000 raise, 0/0xFFFF encode. pytest tests/loadng/test_messages.py: 73 passed.
